source.title: OBLIVIATE: Robust and Practical Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
source.authors: XiaoYu Xu; Min-Xin Du; Qing-Qing Ye; Hai-Bo Hu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates a new unlearning method against relearning, low-bit quantization, and jailbreak attacks, reporting how targeted-knowledge measures change after the attacks.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own WMDP accuracy results, MMLU utility results, Table 6 relearning and int4 quantization outcomes, and the qualitative jailbreak evaluation in Table 9. MIA, fluency, and other utility metrics are not rows because they do not measure the recovery behaviors in the claim. The paper's claims about attack robustness without an outcome, and attack descriptions cited from other work, are not treated as additional results.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a new unlearning method (OBLIVIATE) and tests it against five comparator methods on WMDP. Measures: Bio/Cyber accuracy with no attack (Zephyr-7B, Llama3-8B, Llama3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B); accuracy after relearning on 10% of the forget set; accuracy after int4 quantization (Zephyr-7B only). It also shows qualitative jailbreak examples. These results bear on A (unlearning works), B (relearning), D (quantization), E (jailbreak prompting) and F (a robust counter-method). C is not tested. The reader's V1–V6 map to A–F (V1=A, V2=B, V3=C, V4=D, V5=E, V6=F). The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say OBLIVIATE gives the best trade-off among forget quality, utility and fluency, with state-of-the-art forget quality. They claim it blocks jailbreaks, maintains forgetting under int4 quantization and 'best suppresses' recovery during relearning. That last claim is only relative to the baselines: their own Table 6 shows substantial recovery (Bio 26.9 to 49.2). The abstract also emphasises resistance to membership inference attacks.
record.recipe_differences: OBLIVIATE uses LoRA fine-tuning with vocabulary-level masked loss plus distillation and world-fact losses. Its tested attacks are applied after this method; it is not a replication of the original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured outcome varies by attack type: relearning increases WMDP accuracy substantially, whereas int4 quantization changes it only slightly. Outcomes are also reported across unlearning methods and model families, but the attack evaluation is on Zephyr-7B.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Attack robustness is evaluated on Zephyr-7B only. Relearning uses 10% of the forget set, and quantization tests int4 only. Jailbreak evidence is qualitative and gives no sample count or leakage rate. No never-trained reference model is reported for the attacks, and chance level for WMDP accuracy is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing directly on versions A-F were left out. The paper's other MIA, fluency, and general utility metrics were omitted because they do not measure the specified recovery behavior.

untested.parts: Probe-based recovery as in the original; models above 8B; any attack on the unlearned models other than Zephyr-7B. The paper does not state WMDP's chance level.

Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data; relearning set sizes other than 10% of the forget set; models other than Zephyr-7B; Harry Potter and TOFU; the NPO-family baselines, which were not attacked.
Not tested: no activation-direction ablation and no analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
Bit widths other than int4; models other than Zephyr-7B; non-WMDP datasets; the NPO-family baselines, which keep utility and were not quantized.
Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information. Jailbreaks were run only on OBLIVIATE, not on the comparator methods, and no rate is reported.
Internal-edit attacks; attacks on models other than Zephyr-7B; attacks on Harry Potter and TOFU; a quantified jailbreak success rate.

missing.what: WMDP accuracy and MMLU for the comparator methods with no attack. Zephyr-7B: RMU reaches 30.5/27.3 with MMLU 57.5. NPO, NPO_KL and NPO_GD barely forget (Bio 63.5–64.3 vs 64.4). GA, Adv_GA and RL reach chance, but MMLU falls to 23.0–26.9 and fluency to 1.00. Table 18: RMU barely forgets on Llama3-8B-Instruct (Bio 66.8 vs 71.3). On Mistral-7B, RMU's MMLU falls to 27.1.
Harry Potter forgetting for OBLIVIATE on Llama-2-7B chat: HP-four 25.83 vs Original 37.58 (WHP 33.93); HP-dual 49.64 vs 62.11, near the 50% chance of a 2-option test. MMLU 45.64 vs 46.38.
TOFU forget quality (KS test) for OBLIVIATE: weak forgetting on forget01 and forget05 (2.66E-07, 3.93E-03), strong on forget10 (0.941).
Memorization (DRMA) and MIA metrics after relearning for all attacked methods. DRMA returns to 946.60–985.46 vs Original 1014.67, suggesting near-full recovery of document memorization.
OBLIVIATE's DRMA after relearning is 946.60, vs 128.00 unattacked and Original 1014.67. After int4 it is 129.28, essentially unchanged.

record.verdict_notes: Changes from the earlier verdict: (1) The merge refused it because the record's own versions and rows carry V1–V6. Every row (A1–A12, B1–B12, D1–D12, E1) keeps a row_fixes item with declared identifiers only, decided by what each row measures: V1=A, V2=B, V3=C, V4=D, V5=E, V6=F. Comparator rows lose V6/F. An untested entry for A was added so that every record version has a declared counterpart. (2) A5 changed from partial to observed, and the separate A limits_scope label was dropped: 31.9 is within a point of RMU's 31.2 that the WMDP original called near chance. (3) The B labels are regrouped by size of recovery rather than by Bio/Cyber subset. The earlier grouping put RMU-, ELM-, GA- and RL-cyber (53–72% recovery) under limits_scope while OBLIVIATE-bio (59%) was under supports; now only B8 and B12 (23%, 34%) are limits_scope. (4) The D limits_scope reason now says the GA, Adv_GA and RL models had collapsed before quantization (Table 3 MMLU 23.0/24.8/26.9, fluency 1.00). The earlier text implied GA here matched the setting where quantization recovery was reported. (5) The missing A comparator entry was corrected (RL's MMLU is 26.9, not about 23–25) and RMU's results on the Table 18 models were added. The DRMA entry was split into one entry for B and one for F. Caveats: all attack results are on Zephyr-7B only. No control fine-tunes a model that never had the knowledge on the same 10% relearning data, so new learning cannot be separated from recovery. The cyber forget set is 50 of 400 documents, so cyber relearning likely used very few documents (split not stated). MMLU after the attacks is not reported. The NPO-family baselines were not attacked. The paper does not state WMDP's 25% chance level; it follows from the 4-option format. No instructions to the reader were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures WMDP accuracy and MMLU utility, but does not state a chance level for WMDP; whether the reported accuracy is near chance cannot be determined.
Tests relearning with 10% of the forget set on WMDP only; does not test unrelated or loosely related examples, or other datasets.
No activation-direction ablation or other internal edit test is reported.
Tests 4-bit (int4) quantization on WMDP only; no other bit widths or datasets are reported.
Tests jailbreak prompts on WMDP. Rephrasing alone, other languages, and in-context information are not separately tested.
Tests relearning, int4 quantization, and jailbreaks for OBLIVIATE; does not test internal edits or all attack types named in the claim.
